newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa passes law for Telkom privatisation.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa passes law for Telkom privatisation.

text.p: South Africa's National Assembly passed legislation late on Tuesday to make it possible for the state-owned Telkom telecommunications corporation to sell 30 percent of its equity to a foreign consortium.
The government is selling the stake -- for an estimated six billion rand -- to SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd.
Parliament's adoption of the Post Office Amendment Bill clears the way for the finalisation of the sale, which officials expect to be signed in the next few days.
The amendment cancels a statutory prohibition on the sale of Telkom equity to more than one shareholder and to anyone other than the state.

Deputy President Thabo Mbeki announced on Tuesday that Telkom will get a $1 billion (4.4 billion rand) cash injection following its partial privatisation to pay for a massive roll-out of new phone lines. The balance of the privatisation proceeds will go to the state.
The sale of the stake in the state telecommunications concern is the largest privatisation deal in Sub-Saharan Africa and the first major sell-off in South Africa.
